bug_categories.description: Change the misaligned-access address increment from 32'b100 (+4) to a different value such as 32'b10 (+2) or 32'b1000 (+8), so the second fetch of a split word access targets the wrong address.
bug_categories.applicability: o_wb_ibus_adr = ctrl_misal ? i_ibus_adr + 32'b100 : i_ibus_adr. The upper halfword of a misaligned instruction is fetched from the wrong word, producing corrupted concatenated data.

bug_categories.description: Swap the halves in the concatenation, or capture the wrong half of the bus data (e.g. latch i_wb_ibus_rdt[15:0] into lower_hw instead of [31:16]).
bug_categories.applicability: ibus_rdt_concat = {i_wb_ibus_rdt[15:0], lower_hw} and lower_hw <= i_wb_ibus_rdt[31:16]. Reversing the order or slice yields a wrongly assembled 32-bit instruction on o_ibus_rdt when ctrl_misal is set.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong enable/condition for data capture register
bug_categories.description: Remove or alter the i_wb_ibus_ack gating on lower_hw, e.g. capture every cycle, or capture only when ctrl_misal is set, or add dependence on i_ibus_cyc.
bug_categories.applicability: The always block updating lower_hw only on i_wb_ibus_ack. Capturing without ack overwrites the saved upper halfword with stale or invalid bus data before the second beat arrives, or never captures it during the first beat.

bug_categories.bug_type: Inverted or incorrect ack enable logic
bug_categories.description: Modify the ack_en expression, such as dropping the negation, replacing & with |, or removing the !ctrl_misal term, so acks are suppressed or passed at the wrong time.
bug_categories.applicability: ack_en = !(i_ibus_adr[1] & !ctrl_misal). For halfword-misaligned addresses the first ack should be masked; the bug would forward the ack of the first beat early or block the final ack, causing the master to latch incomplete data or hang.

bug_categories.description: Change how ctrl_misal updates: set to 1 instead of toggling, toggle on i_wb_ibus_ack alone without checking i_ibus_adr[1], or use the wrong address bit (adr[0] or adr[2]).
bug_categories.applicability: else if (i_wb_ibus_ack & i_ibus_adr[1]) ctrl_misal <= !ctrl_misal. The misalignment state machine would fail to return to 0 after the second beat, or toggle on aligned accesses, corrupting subsequent fetches.

bug_categories.description: Remove reset of ctrl_misal, change its reset value to 1, or make reset ineffective (e.g. use !rst), so the design starts or recovers in the wrong state.
bug_categories.applicability: if (rst) ctrl_misal <= 0. A reset value of 1 makes the first fetch use adr+4 and the concatenated data path; ignoring reset leaves ctrl_misal unknown/stale after reset. lower_hw also has no reset and could be affected.

bug_categories.description: Invert the select of the read data or address mux, or swap its inputs, so the concatenated data/offset address is used in the aligned case and raw data in the misaligned case.
bug_categories.applicability: o_ibus_rdt = ctrl_misal ? ibus_rdt_concat : i_wb_ibus_rdt and o_wb_ibus_adr = ctrl_misal ? i_ibus_adr + 4 : i_ibus_adr. Swapping these breaks both aligned and misaligned fetches.

bug_categories.description: Gate o_wb_ibus_cyc with ctrl_misal or ack_en, or drive o_ibus_ack from the wrong term (e.g. i_ibus_cyc instead of i_wb_ibus_ack, or | instead of &).
bug_categories.applicability: o_wb_ibus_cyc = i_ibus_cyc and o_ibus_ack = i_wb_ibus_ack & ack_en. Altering these causes spurious or missing bus cycles and acknowledgments, breaking the Wishbone handshake between master and slave.

mutants.bug_type: Inverted or incorrect ack enable logic

bug_categories.description: The add_b operand is computed as i_op_b ^ {W{i_sub}}; changing the XOR to OR/AND, or inverting the polarity of i_sub (e.g., ^ {W{~i_sub}}), breaks two's complement subtraction so SUB/compare operations produce wrong results.
bug_categories.applicability: Affects add_b and thus result_add, add_cy, result_lt and result_eq. Subtraction, SLT/SLTU and equality comparisons all become incorrect while plain addition still partly works.

bug_categories.description: add_cy_r[0] is loaded with i_sub when i_en is low (the carry-in seed for subtraction at start of a serial op). Changing it to 1'b0, to ~i_sub, or swapping the mux polarity (i_en ? i_sub : add_cy) means the +1 for two's complement is lost or the carry is not propagated between bit-serial cycles.
bug_categories.applicability: Specific to the always block's add_cy_r[0] assignment; in bit-serial operation (W=1) subtraction results would be off by one and multi-cycle carries would be corrupted.

bug_categories.bug_type: Enable gating error on state register
bug_categories.description: cmp_r is updated only when i_en is high. Removing the condition (always update), or inverting it (if(!i_en)), causes the sticky comparison state to be overwritten at wrong times, corrupting equality/less-than accumulation across cycles.
bug_categories.applicability: Applies to 'if(i_en) cmp_r <= o_cmp;'. result_eq and result_slt[0] depend on cmp_r, so multi-cycle compares and SLT results will be wrong.

bug_categories.description: rs1_sx and op_b_sx are masked with i_cmp_sig to select signed vs unsigned compares. Dropping the mask, using ~i_cmp_sig, or taking bit 0 instead of bit B (i_rs1[0]) causes signed/unsigned comparisons to be swapped or wrong for the MSB.
bug_categories.applicability: Affects result_lt computation: rs1_sx + ~op_b_sx + add_cy. SLT vs SLTU behavior will be inverted or incorrect for operands with MSB set.

bug_categories.bug_type: Comparison result mux / equality logic error
bug_categories.description: result_eq = !(|result_add) & (cmp_r | i_cnt0) uses cmp_r to chain equality across serial cycles, with i_cnt0 for first cycle. Changing & to |, changing |result_add to &result_add, dropping the negation, or swapping the o_cmp mux select (i_cmp_eq ? result_lt : result_eq) breaks equality detection.
bug_categories.applicability: Directly modifies result_eq and o_cmp; BEQ/BNE and SLT results would be wrong, e.g., false equality reported when any bit differs in earlier cycles.

bug_categories.description: result_bool combines XOR, OR-like and AND-like terms through i_bool_op[0] and i_bool_op[1]. Swapping the bits, removing the negation of i_bool_op[0], or replacing & with | in the AND term changes the XOR/OR/AND operation mapping (e.g., AND yields OR).
bug_categories.applicability: Specific to the result_bool expression with i_bool_op encoding 00=XOR, 01=OR, 11=AND; operator precedence of &/| mixing makes subtle mistakes feasible.

bug_categories.description: o_rd ORs i_buf with masked result_add, result_slt, result_bool using i_rd_sel[0..2]. Swapping select bit indices (e.g., result_slt using i_rd_sel[2]), or making one AND term an OR, or dropping i_buf, causes wrong result selection or data bleed-through between sources.
bug_categories.applicability: Affects o_rd assignment; instructions selecting add, slt or bool outputs would return the wrong data, and i_buf pass-through (used for shift/other results) would be corrupted.

bug_categories.bug_type: Bit width / indexing mismatch in SLT result
bug_categories.description: result_slt[0] = cmp_r & i_cnt0 and upper bits tied to zero in generate block. Using cmp_r | i_cnt0, placing the result into result_slt[B] instead of bit 0, or making the generate fill with ones/replicating wrong width ({B{...}} vs {W{...}}) puts the SLT bit in the wrong position or sets nonzero upper bits.
bug_categories.applicability: Applies to result_slt assignment and the gen_w_gt_1 block; for W>1 the SLT result must be a 0/1 value in LSB, so misplacement or nonzero upper bits corrupts o_rd.

mutants.bug_type: Comparison result mux / equality logic error
Bit width / indexing mismatch in SLT result

bug_categories.description: Remove the i_en gating on the carry flop so the carry is latched even when the pipeline is stalled (c_r[0] <= c instead of c & i_en), or change the default assignment so upper bits of c_r are not cleared.
bug_categories.applicability: c_r[0] <= c & i_en in the always @(posedge i_clk) block. Without the enable gating, a stale carry propagates into the next bit-serial addition after a stall, corrupting the adder result.

bug_categories.description: Invert or drop the enable masks on the adder operands, e.g. use ~i_rs1_en, drop i_imm_en, or remove the ~clr_lsb mask so the LSB clear never takes effect.
bug_categories.applicability: The adder expression { c, q } = (i_rs1 & {W{i_rs1_en}}) + (i_imm & {W{i_imm_en}} & ~clr_lsb) + c_r. Altering the masks changes the computed address/result, and failing to clear the LSB breaks JALR-style target alignment.

bug_categories.description: Change clr_lsb[0] from i_cnt0 & i_clr_lsb to i_cnt1 & i_clr_lsb, or use OR instead of AND, so the LSB clear occurs on the wrong serial cycle or is always active.
bug_categories.applicability: assign clr_lsb[0] = i_cnt0 & i_clr_lsb. The clear should only apply to the first serial bit when requested; the wrong cycle or operator clears the wrong bit or clears it unconditionally.

bug_categories.description: Modify the bit ranges in the data shift, e.g. data[31:2] <= {..., data[31:3]} changed to data[31:2] or data[30:3], or data[1:0] <= {q, data[1]} changed to use data[0], causing misaligned shifts and lost or duplicated bits.
bug_categories.applicability: W==1 branch: data[31:2] <= { ..., data[31:3] } and data[1:0] <= { (i_init)? q : data[2], data[1] }. Incorrect slicing misaligns the 32-bit shift register and corrupts o_dbus_adr and o_ext_rs1.

bug_categories.description: Change the sign fill from data[31] & i_sh_signed to just data[31] (always sign-extend), to i_sh_signed alone, or use data[30], so logical right shifts incorrectly fill with the sign bit or the wrong bit.
bug_categories.applicability: { W{ data[31] & i_sh_signed } } fill in both W==1 and W==4 branches. This breaks SRL vs SRA distinction in the shifter.

bug_categories.description: Swap the i_init selection so the shift register loads the adder result q when not initializing and shifts in the sign/recirculated bit during init, or change the data[1:0] update condition from i_cnt0 | i_cnt1 to i_cnt0 & i_cnt1 or i_en.
bug_categories.applicability: The (i_init)? q : ... mux and the condition (i_init)? i_cnt0 | i_cnt1 : i_en in the W==1 branch, plus the (i_init)? q mux in the W==4 branch. Wrong polarity or condition prevents operands loading correctly into data.

bug_categories.description: Alter the shift_amount calculation, e.g. swap the right/left shift cases, drop the inversion ~i_shamt[1:0], use i_shamt[2:1], or change the default constant 3'd3 to a different value, so the mux selects the wrong byte/bit window.
bug_categories.applicability: W==4 branch: shift_amount = (!i_shift_op)? 3'd3 : (i_right_shift_op)? 3'd3 + {1'b0,i_shamt[1:0]} : {1'b0,~i_shamt[1:0]}. This feeds the muxdata part-select, so errors produce incorrect shifted results for left and right shifts.

bug_categories.bug_type: MDU output override and lsb capture/tail masking error
bug_categories.description: Change the MDU/i_mdu_op gating on o_lsb (e.g. MDU | i_mdu_op, or forcing 2'b11), alter lsb capture condition (i_cnt0 to i_cnt1 or q[1:0] to q[2:1]), or remove the ~i_cnt_done mask on data_tail so stale bits shift in at the end of the word.
bug_categories.applicability: assign o_lsb = (MDU & i_mdu_op)? 2'b00 : ...; in the W==4 branch lsb <= q[1:0] under i_cnt0 and data_tail <= data[B:1] & {B{~i_cnt_done}}. These errors corrupt the reported LSBs used for alignment/misalignment detection and MDU operation, and the final shifted bits.

bug_categories.description: Change the mask applied to dhi on writes, e.g. invert the polarity of the i_cnt7 term or drop the !cnt_en qualifier, so bit 5 of the counter is cleared at the wrong time.
bug_categories.applicability: In the dhi update, the mask { 2'b11, !(i_shift_op & i_cnt7 & !cnt_en), 5'b11111 } controls clearing of dhi[5]. Changing it to (i_shift_op & i_cnt7 & cnt_en), or removing the negation, breaks the shift-done detection and counter reinitialization.

bug_categories.bug_type: Incorrect boolean condition in enable logic
bug_categories.description: Alter the shift_en expression for shift operations, e.g. change i_init to !i_init, or change (i_bytecnt == 2'b00) to (i_bytecnt == 2'b11), or replace & with |.
bug_categories.applicability: shift_en = i_shift_op ? i_en & i_init & (i_bytecnt == 2'b00) : i_en & byte_valid. A wrong qualifier causes the shift register to load/shift at the wrong cycle or on the wrong byte during shift operations.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong operator precedence / logic in cnt_en
bug_categories.description: Modify cnt_en by changing the AND/OR grouping or inverting terms, e.g. i_shift_op & (!i_init | i_cnt_done) | i_sh_right, or using i_sh_right negated.
bug_categories.applicability: cnt_en = i_shift_op & (!i_init | i_cnt_done & i_sh_right). Changing it makes the counter decrement path (cnt_next) selected at wrong times, which corrupts dhi and the shift amount for right vs. left shifts.

bug_categories.description: Change the decrement amount in cnt_next, e.g. dhi[5:0] - 6'd1 to - 6'd2 or + 6'd1 for W==1, or - 6'd4 to - 6'd2 for W==4.
bug_categories.applicability: In the generate branches, cnt_next uses dhi[5:0] - 6'd1 (W==1) and - 6'd4 (W==4). A wrong step makes the shift amount counter finish early/late, so shifts produce wrong distances and o_sh_done asserts at the wrong time.

bug_categories.description: Shift the slice indices in the data path, e.g. use dhi[6:0] instead of dhi[5:0] in the subtraction, dhi[6] instead of dhi[7] in the W==1 concatenation, or o_dat[W+22:23] in o_q.
bug_categories.applicability: cnt_next = { o_op_b, dhi[7], dhi[5:0]-1 } and the o_q byte-select slices o_dat[W+23:24], [W+15:16], [W+7:8], [W-1:0] are index-sensitive; off-by-one slices corrupt the counter, the propagated bit, or the selected output byte lane.

bug_categories.description: Swap the inputs of a mux or invert its select, e.g. o_op_b = i_op_b_sel ? i_imm : i_rs2, or swap cnt_next and the shifted value in dat_shamt, or swap the i_load data/shift paths.
bug_categories.applicability: o_op_b selects between i_rs2 and i_imm; dat_shamt selects between cnt_next and { o_op_b, dhi[7:W] } on cnt_en; the dhi register chooses between i_dat[31:24] and dat_shamt on i_load. Swapping any of these routes wrong operands into the shift register.

bug_categories.bug_type: Shift direction / data path error in dlo
bug_categories.description: Change the shift-in data of dlo, e.g. { dhi[B:0], dlo[23:W] } to { dlo[B:0], dhi[...] }, use dlo[22:W-1], or shift left instead of right.
bug_categories.applicability: dlo <= { dhi[B:0], dlo[23:W] } implements the serial right shift across the 32-bit dhi/dlo register. Altering the concatenation order or slice breaks bit propagation between dhi and dlo, corrupting o_dat and o_q.

bug_categories.bug_type: Byte lane select / decode error in o_q and byte_valid
bug_categories.description: Swap the i_lsb decode values in o_q (e.g. 2'd3 and 2'd2 swapped) or change a term in byte_valid such as !i_bytecnt[1] & !i_lsb[1] to use i_lsb[0].
bug_categories.applicability: o_q ORs four AND-masked byte lanes keyed on i_lsb == 0..3, and byte_valid is a sum-of-products over i_lsb and i_bytecnt bits. Incorrect decode returns the wrong byte lane or enables dlo/dhi shifting on invalid bytes during load/store alignment.

mutants.bug_type: Wrong operator precedence / logic in cnt_en

bug_categories.bug_type: Inverted control logic on illegal instruction output mux
bug_categories.description: The output select `assign o_instr = (illegal_instr) ? i_instr : comp_instr;` is inverted or the registered flag polarity is flipped (`o_iscomp <= illegal_instr` instead of `!illegal_instr`), so legal compressed instructions pass through unexpanded and illegal ones are treated as compressed.
bug_categories.applicability: Affects every instruction: o_instr and o_iscomp would be wrong for both the 32-bit pass-through path (i_instr[1:0]==2'b11) and all compressed expansions.

bug_categories.bug_type: Missing or altered enable condition on sequential update
bug_categories.description: The `if(i_ack)` gating on o_iscomp is removed, changed to `!i_ack`, or the register is updated on a different condition, so o_iscomp changes when no acknowledge is present or fails to update when it is.
bug_categories.applicability: o_iscomp is the only register and is loaded only when i_ack is high. A wrong enable causes it to lose sync with the instruction stream and mismatch the held instruction.

bug_categories.bug_type: Incorrect bit-slice selection of immediate fields
bug_categories.description: Immediate bits in the expansion are permuted or off by one, e.g. in C.ADDI4SPN swapping `i_instr[10:7]` with `i_instr[12:11]`, or in C.LW/C.SW using `i_instr[5]` and `i_instr[6]` in the wrong order, producing wrong offsets.
bug_categories.applicability: The RVC immediate encodings are heavily scrambled (C.ADDI4SPN, C.LW, C.SW, C.JAL/C.J, C.LUI/C.ADDI16SP, C.LWSP, C.SWSP, branch offsets), so a swapped or shifted index yields valid Verilog but wrong decoded immediates.

bug_categories.description: The replication count of `i_instr[12]` is changed, e.g. `{ 6{i_instr[12]} }` to `{ 5{...} }` with compensating bits, or sign extension replaced with zero extension in C.ADDI, C.LI, C.ANDI, C.LUI, C.JAL or C.BEQZ/C.BNEZ, giving wrong signed immediates for negative values.
bug_categories.applicability: Used in C.ADDI, C.LI, C.ANDI, C.JAL/C.J (`{9{i_instr[12]}}`), C.LUI (`{15{...}}`), C.ADDI16SP (`{3{...}}`) and branches (`{4{...}}`). Replication changes keep the concatenation valid if widths are balanced but corrupt sign behavior.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong opcode or funct3 constant in expanded instruction
bug_categories.description: A localparam value or inline funct3 is swapped, e.g. OPCODE_LOAD used for a store expansion, OPCODE_OP_IMM replaced with OPCODE_OP, C.AND funct3 3'b111 changed to 3'b110 (OR), or C.XOR/C.OR funct3 values exchanged.
bug_categories.applicability: Many expansions use localparam opcodes and literal funct3 fields (SRLI/SRAI 3'b101, ANDI 3'b111, SUB/XOR/OR/AND, LW/SW 3'b010, SLLI 3'b001); each is a single-token edit that silently changes the instruction semantics.

bug_categories.bug_type: Incorrect case selector decode / swapped case items
bug_categories.description: Case labels are altered, e.g. in the quadrant 0 case swapping `2'b10` (illegal/reserved) with `2'b11` for C.SW, merging 3'b001 and 3'b101 incorrectly, or changing the `i_instr[11:10]` and `i_instr[6:5]` decode in the arithmetic group, so instructions map to the wrong expansion or illegal flag.
bug_categories.applicability: The nested case structure on i_instr[1:0], [15:14], [15:13], [11:10], [6:5] has many arms; changing one label or selector slice reroutes decoding while still compiling.

bug_categories.bug_type: Missing or wrong illegal-instruction flag assignment
bug_categories.description: illegal_instr is not set (or is set wrongly) for specific cases: dropping `illegal_instr = 1'b1` for the reserved quadrant-0 encoding 2'b10, or for 2'b11 (32-bit instructions), or setting it for valid compressed cases, so o_iscomp and o_instr select are wrong.
bug_categories.applicability: illegal_instr is only asserted in two places (quadrant 0 funct 2'b10 and quadrant 3). Removing or altering them causes 32-bit instructions to be treated as compressed or reserved encodings to be expanded.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong register field / hard-coded register constant in expansion
bug_categories.description: The fixed register numbers are changed, e.g. `5'h02` (sp) replaced with `5'h01` (ra) in C.ADDI4SPN/C.LWSP/C.SWSP/C.ADDI16SP, the `5'b00001` link register in C.JALR changed to x0, or the compressed register prefix `2'b01` (x8-x15) dropped or changed to `2'b00`.
bug_categories.applicability: RVC expansions rely on hard-coded sp/ra/x0 and the `2'b01` prefix for 3-bit register fields (C.LW, C.SW, C.AND, C.SUB etc.); altering any yields the wrong source/destination register.

mutants.bug_type: Missing or altered enable condition on sequential update
Wrong opcode or funct3 constant in expanded instruction
Wrong register field / hard-coded register constant in expansion

bug_categories.description: Invert the reset strategy check or drop one register from the reset block, so reset no longer clears o_new_irq or mie_mtie as intended.
bug_categories.applicability: In the final `if(i_rst) if(RESET_STRATEGY != "NONE")` block, change the condition to `== "NONE"`, or remove `mie_mtie <= 1'b0`. After reset, mie_mtie or o_new_irq would hold stale or X values, which could cause spurious timer interrupts. Alternatively, move the reset block ahead of the functional assignments so it is overridden by them.

bug_categories.bug_type: Edge detection / interrupt pulse logic error
bug_categories.description: Break the rising-edge detection that generates a one-shot new IRQ by removing the inversion or changing the register it samples.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `o_new_irq <= timer_irq & !timer_irq_r` to `timer_irq & timer_irq_r` or `timer_irq | !timer_irq_r`. Alternatively, update timer_irq_r outside the `i_trig_irq` gate. The IRQ would then fire continuously, never fire, or fire at the wrong time.

bug_categories.bug_type: Incorrect boolean condition in interrupt enable
bug_categories.description: Alter the AND combination of mtip, global MIE and timer-enable MTIE so that a masked interrupt can fire or an enabled one is suppressed.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `timer_irq = i_mtip & mstatus_mie & mie_mtie` to use `|` for one term or drop `mie_mtie`. The timer interrupt would then be raised when the global or timer interrupt enable is cleared.

bug_categories.description: Swap or corrupt the CSR write-data operations for SET/CLR/EXT so that the CSR write semantic is wrong.
bug_categories.applicability: In the `csr_in` assignment, change `csr_out | d` (SET) to `csr_out & d`, change `csr_out & ~d` (CLR) to `csr_out & d` or `csr_out | ~d`, or swap the CSR_SOURCE_SET and CSR_SOURCE_CLR localparam encodings. CSRRS/CSRRC instructions would then modify the wrong bits.

bug_categories.description: Use the wrong bit position when sampling serial or parallel CSR data into the single-bit state registers.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `csr_in[B]` to `csr_in[0]` for `mie_mtie`, `mstatus_mie` or `mcause31`. Alternatively alter the `csr_in[(W == 1)? 0 : 2]` and `csr_in[(W == 1)? 0 : 1]` indices in mcause3_0[2]/[1], or the mstatus W==4 concatenation `{ i_cnt11 | ..., 2'b00, i_cnt12 }`. With W=4 the data would be captured from the wrong bit, and with W=1 these indexes are equal, so the bug would only show up for wider configurations.

bug_categories.description: Corrupt the stacking of the interrupt-enable bit on trap entry and its restoration on mret.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `mstatus_mie <= !i_trap & ((i_mret)? mstatus_mpie : csr_in[B])` so mret selects csr_in[B] and the non-mret case selects mstatus_mpie, or remove `!i_trap` so MIE is not cleared on trap. Alternatively, update mstatus_mpie on `i_mret` rather than on `i_trap & i_cnt_done`, or save `!mstatus_mie`. Nested interrupt handling would then break.

bug_categories.description: Use the wrong bit-counter strobe or drop an enable qualifier in a register's write condition, so updates happen at the wrong serial time slot or when not enabled.
bug_categories.applicability: Replace `i_cnt7` with `i_cnt3` in the `mie_mtie` write enable, swap `i_cnt_done` with `i_cnt0to3` in the mcause update conditions, or drop `& i_en` from the `mstatus_mie` or mcause write enables. Registers would capture the wrong serial bit or update when the pipeline is stalled.

bug_categories.description: Corrupt the mcause code bits or the read-back mux so the exception cause is reported wrongly.
bug_categories.applicability: Modify mcause3_0[3] to `i_e_op | !i_ebreak`, remove `i_mem_cmd` from mcause3_0[1], and swap `o_new_irq` with `timer_irq` in the mcause31 interrupt flag (`(i_trap)? o_new_irq : csr_in[B]`). Another option is to swap the priority of `i_cnt0to3` and `i_cnt_done` in the `mcause` mux, or to drop `i_mcause_en & i_en` gating in the `csr_out` OR-tree. The software would then see an incorrect cause code or interrupt flag.

bug_categories.description: The pc_plus_4_cy_r register's enable gating is altered, e.g., removing the i_pc_en qualifier or dropping the carry, so that carry propagates between serial bit-slices incorrectly or stale carry is retained when the PC is not advancing.
bug_categories.applicability: In the always block, change `pc_plus_4_cy_r <= i_pc_en & pc_plus_4_cy;` to `pc_plus_4_cy_r <= pc_plus_4_cy;` (or similarly for pc_plus_offset_cy_r). The carry then leaks into the next instruction's first cycle when i_pc_en is low, corrupting pc+4 and branch target computation.

bug_categories.description: The plus_4 increment selection for compressed vs. non-compressed instructions is inverted or uses the wrong counter bit, so PC advances by 2 vs 4 incorrectly.
bug_categories.applicability: In gen_plus_4_w_eq_1, change `(i_iscomp)? i_cnt1 : i_cnt2` to `(i_iscomp)? i_cnt2 : i_cnt1`, or in the W==4 branch swap the 2 and 4 constants or use `i_cnt0 & i_cnt1` instead of `|`. Sequential PC update will then be off by 2 bytes.

bug_categories.bug_type: Shift/concatenation error in PC shift register
bug_categories.description: The serial shift of new_pc into o_ibus_adr uses the wrong slice boundaries, causing bit misalignment or loss of the upper bits of the PC after a full word is shifted in.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `{ new_pc, o_ibus_adr[31:W] }` to `{ new_pc, o_ibus_adr[30:W-1] }` or `{ o_ibus_adr[W-1:0], new_pc }`/`o_ibus_adr[31:W+1]`, which breaks the right-shift register behavior for both the NONE and non-NONE reset branches.

bug_categories.description: Reset behavior is changed so that reset value or priority is wrong: reset is ignored unless i_pc_en is set, loads the wrong value, or the reset-vs-enable priority is swapped.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `if(i_pc_en | i_rst)` to `if(i_pc_en & i_rst)` or `(i_rst)? RESET_PC : ...` to `(i_pc_en)? {new_pc, ...} : RESET_PC`; alternatively, apply `RESET_PC[31:W]` or drop reset in the non-NONE strategy so o_ibus_adr is not reliably initialized to RESET_PC.

bug_categories.description: The masking applied to i_csr_pc during a trap in the first cycles is wrong, so the low bits (alignment bits) of the trap vector are not cleared or are cleared at the wrong time.
bug_categories.applicability: In gen_new_pc_w_eq_1, change `!(i_cnt0 || i_cnt1)` to `!(i_cnt0 && i_cnt1)` or `!i_cnt0`; in the W==4 branch change `4'b1100` to `4'b1110` or swap the constants. Trap target addresses become misaligned or wrongly masked.

bug_categories.bug_type: Priority/mux ordering error in next-PC selection
bug_categories.description: The priority between trap, jump, and sequential PC is reordered, so a jump overrides a trap or the wrong source is selected.
bug_categories.applicability: Swap the ternary order in new_pc: `(i_jump)? pc_plus_offset_aligned : (i_trap)? i_csr_pc & ... : pc_plus_4`, or invert the condition `i_jump` to `!i_jump`. Traps taken in the same cycle as jumps will jump to the wrong address.

bug_categories.bug_type: Alignment masking error on jump target
bug_categories.description: The LSB clearing of the computed jump target (needed for JALR) is applied with the wrong condition or removed, so odd addresses are not aligned properly.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `pc_plus_offset[0] & !i_cnt0` to `pc_plus_offset[0] & !i_cnt1`, remove the mask, or use `| !i_cnt0`. This affects o_bad_pc and new_pc on jumps, and misaligned targets are not detected or cleared correctly.

bug_categories.bug_type: Operand selection / rd output logic error
bug_categories.description: The operand selection for the offset adder or the rd result mux uses wrong control signals or operators, producing wrong link/AUIPC/LUI values.
bug_categories.applicability: Change `offset_b = (i_utype)? i_imm & {W{i_cnt12to31}} : i_buf` to use `!i_cnt12to31` or swap i_imm and i_buf; change `offset_a = {W{i_pc_rel}} & pc` to `{W{!i_pc_rel}} & pc`; or in o_rd change `|` to `&`, or swap i_utype and i_jal_or_jalr, so AUIPC/LUI/JAL link values are wrong.

mutants.bug_type: Priority/mux ordering error in next-PC selection
Shift/concatenation error in PC shift register

bug_categories.description: The shared-register enable conditions use 'i_wb_en | i_cnt_en & i_immdec_en[x]' where & binds tighter than |. Changing the grouping to '(i_wb_en | i_cnt_en) & i_immdec_en[x]' would block write-back loads whenever the immdec enable bit is low, or replacing | with & would break loading.
bug_categories.applicability: gen_shared_imm_regs always block: enables for imm19_12_20, imm30_25, imm24_20 and imm11_7. Write-back of the instruction fields would become dependent on i_immdec_en, corrupting rd/rs1/rs2 addresses and immediates.

bug_categories.description: Alter the bit that feeds the MSB of a shift register, e.g. use imm11_7[0] instead of imm30_25[0] for imm24_20's serial input, or imm19_12_20[0] swapped with imm24_20[0], breaking the serial immediate bit ordering.
bug_categories.applicability: Shift chains in imm24_20, imm11_7, imm30_25, and imm19_12_20 in both the shared and separate register variants, and the equivalent i-register chains in the W=4 branch (e.g. i27 <= i20 vs i15).

bug_categories.description: Remove or invert the CSR immediate masking in signbit (e.g. 'imm31 | !i_csr_imm_en' or 'imm31 & i_csr_imm_en'), or select signbit under the wrong ctrl bit, so sign extension is wrong or CSR immediates get sign-extended.
bug_categories.applicability: The signbit wire in both generate branches, plus its use in imm7 <= signbit, o_imm when i_cnt_done, and the i_ctrl[3]/[2]/[1] muxes feeding the MSB of the shift registers.

bug_categories.description: Swap the polarity or priority of the i_ctrl-based muxes, e.g. '(i_ctrl[2]) ? imm7 : (i_ctrl[1]) ? signbit : imm19_12_20[0]' reordered so i_ctrl[1] has priority, or i_ctrl[0] selection between imm11_7[0] and imm24_20[0] swapped.
bug_categories.applicability: imm30_25 shift input mux, imm19_12_20 input mux using i_ctrl[3], o_imm output mux (i_cnt_done / i_ctrl[0] priority) in W=1, and o_imm[3:0], i27, i30, i29, i28 muxes in W=4.

bug_categories.bug_type: Bit-slice / field mapping error in write-back load
bug_categories.description: Load the wrong bit range from i_wb_rdt, such as rs1_addr <= i_wb_rdt[24:20] or imm19_12_20 <= {i_wb_rdt[20], i_wb_rdt[19:12]}, or off-by-one slice like i_wb_rdt[10:6].
bug_categories.applicability: i_wb_en loads for rd_addr, rs1_addr, rs2_addr, imm19_12_20, imm30_25, imm11_7 in the shared/separate W=1 variants, and the individual i* bit loads in the W=4 branch (e.g. i18 <= i_wb_rdt[17], i7_2 <= i_wb_rdt[8]).

bug_categories.description: Change the bit index used for output assignments, e.g. o_csr_imm = imm19_12_20[3] instead of [4], o_rs1_addr = imm19_12_20[7:3], or in W=4 mapping o_csr_imm[3:0] to i17..i14 instead of i18..i15.
bug_categories.applicability: o_csr_imm and o_rs1_addr assignments in gen_immdec_w_eq_1, o_csr_imm[3:0] assignments and o_imm[3:0] tap selection (i10/i23, i9/i22, i8/i21, i7_2/i20_2) in gen_immdec_w_eq_4.

bug_categories.description: In the separate-register variant, the i_cnt_en block follows the i_wb_en block, so the shift wins when both are asserted. Reordering them or making them mutually exclusive via else changes which update takes precedence; similarly drop i_wb_en from the shared-register ternary priority.
bug_categories.applicability: gen_separate_imm_regs and gen_immdec_w_eq_4 always blocks where i_wb_en and i_cnt_en nonblocking assignments to the same registers (imm19_12_20, imm7, imm30_25, imm24_20, imm11_7, i10, i23, etc.) are ordered; also the '(i_wb_en)? load : shift' ternaries in the shared variant.

bug_categories.bug_type: Missing/incorrect register update in duplicate or shadow registers
bug_categories.description: Omit or mis-wire the update of shadow registers used for the duplicated bits, e.g. remove i7_2 <= i11 or i20_2 <= i24 from the shift block, feed i7_2 from i7, or drop the i_wb_en load of i7_2/i20_2, and in W=1 drop the enable for imm7 so it no longer updates on i_cnt_en.
bug_categories.applicability: W=4 duplicates i7_2, i20_2 (used for o_imm[0]) and the sibling shift taps i10/i23, i9/i22, i8/i21; W=1 imm7 update 'if(i_wb_en | i_cnt_en) imm7 <= ...' which feeds imm30_25's MSB under i_ctrl[2].

mutants.bug_type: Missing/incorrect register update in duplicate or shadow registers

bug_categories.description: Change the OR combination in dat_valid to AND (e.g., i_mdu_op & i_word) or drop one of the terms, so data validity is computed incorrectly.
bug_categories.applicability: dat_valid = i_mdu_op | i_word | (i_bytecnt == 2'b00) | i_half & !i_bytecnt[1] controls both the o_rd mux and the signbit capture, so wrong operators cause incorrect pass-through of bufreg2_q versus sign extension.

bug_categories.description: Alter grouping so the AND/OR precedence changes, e.g., (i_word | i_half) & !i_bytecnt[1], or (i_half | i_lsb[1]) in wb_sel[3].
bug_categories.applicability: dat_valid and o_wb_sel[3]/o_wb_sel[1] mix | and & without parentheses (i_half & !i_bytecnt[1], i_half & i_lsb[1]), so regrouping subtly changes half-word behavior.

bug_categories.description: Remove or add an inversion on a bit, e.g., change !i_bytecnt[1] to i_bytecnt[1] or !i_lsb[1] to i_lsb[1].
bug_categories.applicability: The half-word terms in dat_valid and o_wb_sel[1] depend on the polarity of i_bytecnt[1] and i_lsb[1]; flipping them selects the wrong byte lanes/halfword validity.

bug_categories.description: Change a 2-bit comparison constant, e.g., i_lsb == 2'b10 to 2'b01 in o_wb_sel[2], or i_bytecnt == 2'b00 to 2'b01.
bug_categories.applicability: o_wb_sel[3:0] use one-hot-like decodes of i_lsb (11,10,01,00) and dat_valid uses i_bytecnt == 2'b00; altering constants causes duplicate or missing byte-select assertions.

bug_categories.description: Swap bit selects or signals, e.g., signbit <= i_bufreg2_q[0] instead of [B], or o_wb_sel[3] uses i_lsb[0] instead of i_lsb[1], or swap i_word and i_half.
bug_categories.applicability: Sign capture relies on i_bufreg2_q[B] (MSB); o_wb_sel and o_misalign rely on specific i_lsb[1]/i_lsb[0] bits, so index mistakes break sign extension and lane selection.

bug_categories.description: Modify the fill value in the non-valid branch of o_rd, e.g., use { W{ i_signed | signbit } }, drop i_signed, or use ~signbit, or replicate only a single bit instead of W.
bug_categories.applicability: o_rd = dat_valid ? i_bufreg2_q : {W{i_signed & signbit}} implements serial sign extension; altering the AND or polarity yields wrong extension for signed vs unsigned loads.

bug_categories.description: Change the signbit register update condition or timing, e.g., update unconditionally, update on !dat_valid, use negedge i_clk, or add a nonblocking vs blocking mismatch.
bug_categories.applicability: signbit is only latched when dat_valid is true; changing the enable makes the sign bit sampled from invalid data, corrupting sign extension of subsequent bytes.

bug_categories.description: Change the o_misalign expression, e.g., swap i_word/i_half in terms, use i_lsb[1] & i_half, replace WITH_CSR & with |, or omit the i_lsb[0] term.
bug_categories.applicability: o_misalign = WITH_CSR & (i_lsb[0] & (i_word | i_half) | i_lsb[1] & i_word) must flag unaligned word/halfword accesses; wrong terms either miss misaligned accesses or flag aligned ones, and the WITH_CSR gating can be defeated.

bug_categories.description: The x0 write-suppression logic is broken so writes to register 0 are allowed or legitimate writes are blocked. For example, change rd_wen = i_rd_wen & |i_rd_waddr to use &i_rd_waddr (AND-reduction) or drop the |i_rd_waddr term.
bug_categories.applicability: rd_wen feeds o_wen0 in both the gen_csr and gen_no_csr branches. With &i_rd_waddr, only writes to x31 would be enabled and x0 would be writable, corrupting the register file.

bug_categories.description: The i_trap select on the write-path muxes is swapped or applied inconsistently. For example, o_wdata0 = i_trap ? rd : mtval, or o_wreg0 selects the trap address when i_trap is low.
bug_categories.applicability: o_wdata0, o_wdata1, o_wreg0 and o_wreg1 in gen_csr all use i_trap to choose between CSR trap writes (mtval, mepc) and normal rd/CSR writes. Inverting any one of them sends trap data to the wrong register or sends normal data to the CSR register.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong constant CSR register address encoding
bug_categories.description: The constant register-index encodings for trap writes are altered, e.g. swapping 6'b100011 and 6'b100010, or changing a bit so mtval and mepc are written to the wrong CSR slots.
bug_categories.applicability: o_wreg0 = 6'b100011 (mtval) and o_wreg1 = 6'b100010 (mepc) on trap. Swapping them or flipping a bit makes mepc/mtval land in the wrong registers. The { 4'b1000, i_csr_addr } prefix could also be changed to 4'b1001.

bug_categories.description: The i_cnt_en gating or the trap/enable OR terms in the write enables are changed. For example, drop i_cnt_en from o_wen1, replace | with & in (i_trap | rd_wen), or use i_mret instead of i_csr_en.
bug_categories.applicability: o_wen0 = i_cnt_en & (i_trap | rd_wen) and o_wen1 = i_cnt_en & (i_trap | i_csr_en). Without i_cnt_en the bit-serial writes happen on every cycle. With & instead of |, trap writes would need rd_wen as well, so mtval would be lost when rd_wen is 0.

bug_categories.description: The one-hot AND-OR mux that forms rd is corrupted: an enable is swapped with the wrong source, a term is dropped, or the replication is changed. For example, i_rd_csr_en gates i_mem_rd, or i_ctrl_rd is gated by an enable instead of always OR-ed in.
bug_categories.applicability: rd in gen_csr combines {W{i_rd_alu_en}}&i_alu_rd, {W{i_rd_csr_en}}&i_csr_rd, {W{i_rd_mem_en}}&i_mem_rd and i_ctrl_rd. The gen_no_csr rd has the same structure. Mis-pairing enables writes the wrong result data to the register file.

bug_categories.description: The complex concatenation that builds o_rreg1 is mis-specified. Examples are using i_rs2_raddr[4:2] with the wrong mask polarity, swapping the i_trap and i_mret bit positions, or changing the sel_rs2 inversion so the CSR-bank select bit is wrong.
bug_categories.applicability: o_rreg1 = {~sel_rs2, rs2[4:2]&{3{sel_rs2}}, {1'b0,i_trap}|{i_mret,1'b0}|{2{i_csr_en}}&i_csr_addr|{2{sel_rs2}}&rs2[1:0]}. Swapping trap and mret selects the wrong CSR (mepc vs. other) for reads, and a wrong sel_rs2 breaks normal rs2 reads.

bug_categories.description: The condition that chooses a normal rs2 read versus a CSR/mepc read is changed, e.g. dropping i_csr_en or i_mret from the OR, or changing the OR to AND.
bug_categories.applicability: sel_rs2 = !(i_trap | i_mret | i_csr_en). If i_mret is dropped, mret reads the regular rs2 register instead of mepc and o_csr_pc returns the wrong return address. If OR becomes AND, sel_rs2 is nearly always 1 and CSR reads are broken.

bug_categories.bug_type: Output masking / width and parameter handling error
bug_categories.description: The masking and replication on outputs is wrong. For example, remove the { W{i_csr_en} } mask from o_csr, use a single-bit i_csr_en instead of replication, or wire o_csr_pc to i_rdata0 instead of i_rdata1. Parameter-dependent widths such as [4+WITH_CSR:0] or the |WITH_CSR generate condition can also be altered.
bug_categories.applicability: o_csr = i_rdata1 & {W{i_csr_en}} must be zero when no CSR operation occurs. Dropping the mask leaks read data into the CSR path. With W>1, a non-replicated i_csr_en masks only bit 0. o_csr_pc, o_rs1 and o_rs2 can be cross-connected between i_rdata0 and i_rdata1, and the generate-condition or width changes break the CSR vs. non-CSR configurations.

mutants.bug_type: Output masking / width and parameter handling error

bug_categories.description: Change the lower bound of the slice used to compute regzero from 5-$clog2(width) to a different value (e.g., 4-$clog2(width) or 6-$clog2(width)), so the CSR/zero-register region is detected over the wrong address range.
bug_categories.applicability: regzero <= !(|i_raddr[$clog2(depth)-1:5-$clog2(width)]) determines which read addresses are forced to zero. Shifting the bound makes the masked region too large or too small, so reads of the first 32 registers return wrong data.

bug_categories.description: Remove or add the logical negation in the regzero computation (use |i_raddr[...] instead of !(|i_raddr[...])), so masking applies to the wrong addresses.
bug_categories.applicability: regzero is meant to be 1 only when the upper address bits are all zero. Inverting it zeroes o_rdata for all other addresses and passes data for the zero region.

bug_categories.description: Change the output mask from rdata & ~{width{regzero}} to use OR, XOR, or a non-inverted mask (rdata & {width{regzero}}), or drop the mask entirely.
bug_categories.applicability: o_rdata is formed by masking rdata with regzero. Changing the operator or inversion breaks the guarantee that register-zero reads return 0 and corrupts normal read data.

bug_categories.description: Change regzero from non-blocking registered to a combinational assign based on the current i_raddr, or add an extra pipeline stage, so it is no longer aligned with the registered rdata.
bug_categories.applicability: rdata is registered with one cycle latency and regzero is registered to match. A combinational or delayed regzero masks the wrong read's data when i_raddr changes between cycles.

bug_categories.description: Use i_raddr for the memory write index or i_waddr for the memory read index.
bug_categories.applicability: The always block uses memory[i_waddr] for writes and memory[i_raddr] for reads. Swapping them causes writes to land at the read address and reads to fetch from the write address.

bug_categories.description: Remove, invert, or swap the enable conditions: write unconditionally, use !i_wen, or gate the read with i_wen instead of i_ren.
bug_categories.applicability: Writes are gated by i_wen and read data selection by i_ren. Incorrect gating causes spurious memory writes or loss of valid read data when i_ren is asserted.

bug_categories.description: Change the memory write from non-blocking (<=) to blocking (=), altering read-after-write behavior when i_waddr equals i_raddr in the same cycle.
bug_categories.applicability: With blocking assignment placed before the read statement in the same always block, a simultaneous read of the written address returns the new data instead of the old data, changing the memory's read-first semantics.

bug_categories.description: Alter the default depth calculation, e.g. use 32 * (32 - csr_regs) / width or drop the csr_regs term, or change the $clog2(depth) address width used in ports.
bug_categories.applicability: depth = 32*(32+csr_regs)/width sets memory size and address widths. A wrong formula yields too small a memory, address truncation, and a mismatched regzero slice, so high addresses alias or are lost.

bug_categories.description: Change the write counter derivation `wcnt = rcnt - 4` to a different offset (e.g., rcnt - 3 or rcnt - 5), shifting the write phase relative to the read phase.
bug_categories.applicability: wcnt drives wtrig1 (ratio==2), the write address low bits (wcnt[CMSB:l2r]) and the wen0_r/wen1_r capture condition (wcnt[0]), so a wrong offset causes writes to land at wrong addresses/times and register data to be written to the wrong RAM word.

bug_categories.bug_type: Mux select inversion / wrong select signal
bug_categories.description: Invert or swap the select of the read register mux: `rreg = rtrig0 ? i_rreg1 : i_rreg0` becomes `rtrig0 ? i_rreg0 : i_rreg1` or uses rtrig1 instead of rtrig0.
bug_categories.applicability: The read address presented to RAM would fetch rs1 when rs2 is expected (and vice versa), corrupting o_rdata0/o_rdata1 while the design remains structurally valid.

bug_categories.description: Change the rtrig0 compare `rcnt[l2r-1:0] == 1` to `== 0` or `== 2`, or change the o_ren condition `rcnt[l2r-1:1] == 0` to compare against a different value.
bug_categories.applicability: rtrig0 times the capture of i_rdata into rdata0 and the read-address mux switch, and rtrig1 is derived from it; shifting it misaligns captured read data by a cycle and breaks the serial bit stream outputs and RAM read enable pulse.

bug_categories.description: Remove one of the registers from the reset block (e.g., omit rgate, rgnt, or rcnt reset) or invert the reset_strategy condition so reset is applied under the wrong strategy.
bug_categories.applicability: With reset_strategy MINI, rgate/rgnt/rreq_r/rcnt are reset; leaving rgnt or rgate unreset can leave o_ready/o_ren asserted after reset, and a nonzero rcnt starts the sequencer in a bad phase.

bug_categories.description: Alter the write data shift-in: `wdata0_r <= { i_wdata0, wdata0_r[width-1:W] }` becomes `{ wdata0_r[width-W-1:0], i_wdata0 }` (shift the opposite way) or the slice of wdata1_r is mis-sized.
bug_categories.applicability: The serial-to-parallel write data assembly would produce bit-reversed or misaligned words in o_wdata, and wdata1_r's extra W bits are used as a delay stage, so changing it corrupts the second register write.

bug_categories.bug_type: Counter load value error on request
bug_categories.description: Modify the load of rcnt on request `{ {CMSB-1{1'b0}}, i_wreq, 1'b0 }` so i_wreq and the constant are swapped or the load uses i_rreq instead, or the increment `+1` is changed to `+2`.
bug_categories.applicability: rcnt start value encodes whether a read or write sequence begins (2 for write, 0 for read); incorrect loading shifts the whole read/write schedule, and wrong increment skips phases and breaks address generation.

bug_categories.description: Change `o_ready = rgnt | i_wreq` to `rgnt & i_wreq` or alter rgnt pipeline (`rgnt <= rreq_r` to `rgnt <= i_rreq`), shortening or lengthening the read latency.
bug_categories.applicability: o_ready tells the CPU when read data is available; premature or never-asserted ready causes the core to consume stale rdata or stall, and writes would not be acknowledged immediately.

bug_categories.description: Change `o_wen = wtrig0 & wen0_r | wtrig1 & wen1_r` so that terms are mixed (wtrig0 & wen1_r | wtrig1 & wen0_r), or change the latching condition `if(wcnt[0])` to `if(!wcnt[0])`.
bug_categories.applicability: Write enables for the two register-write ports would be swapped or captured at wrong times, causing the wrong port's write to be committed or writes to occur when disabled (e.g., writing to x0-like disabled targets) and RAM contents to be corrupted.

mutants.bug_type: Counter load value error on request

bug_categories.description: In take_branch, the expression `!i_cond_branch | i_alu_cmp ^ i_bne_or_bge` relies on XOR binding tighter than OR. Changing it to `(!i_cond_branch | i_alu_cmp) ^ i_bne_or_bge`, or replacing XOR with AND/OR, alters branch decisions.
bug_categories.applicability: Affects take_branch, which drives o_ctrl_jump, trap_pending, o_rf_wreq and o_bufreg_en. Conditional branches would be taken or skipped incorrectly, and unconditional branches could fail.

bug_categories.description: Change one of the 3-bit comparison constants in the counter-position decodes, e.g. o_cnt7 compares o_cnt[4:2] == 3'd2 instead of 3'd1, o_cnt11 uses 3'd3, or o_cnt_done uses 3'b110 instead of 3'b111.
bug_categories.applicability: o_cnt7, o_cnt11, o_cnt12 and o_cnt_done are derived from o_cnt[4:2] and cnt_r. A wrong constant makes the signals fire in the wrong cycle, ending the 32-bit serial operation early or late and corrupting all downstream timing.

bug_categories.description: Remove or alter the reset of state registers: omit init_done or o_ctrl_jump reset, invert the RESET_STRATEGY != "NONE" condition, reset cnt_lsb to 4'b0001 instead of 0, or drop the o_cnt reset in a generate branch.
bug_categories.applicability: The reset block covers init_done, o_ctrl_jump, o_cnt, cnt_lsb and cnt_en. A bad reset leaves the counter or init state wrong after i_rst, causing a spurious or stuck serial cycle.

bug_categories.description: In the W==1 branch, change the cnt_lsb shift to `{cnt_lsb[3:1], cnt_lsb[0] & !o_cnt_done | i_rf_ready}` or `{cnt_lsb[2:0], cnt_lsb[3] | i_rf_ready}`, or remove the !o_cnt_done term.
bug_categories.applicability: cnt_lsb is the one-hot ring that generates cnt_r and o_cnt_en. A wrong feedback path produces a counter that never stops, never advances, or yields wrong cnt_r phases, breaking o_cnt0..o_cnt3 and o_cnt_done.

bug_categories.description: Change `o_cnt + {2'd0, cnt_r[3]}` to increment on cnt_r[0] or by a different value, or use `{2'd0, cnt_en}` incorrectly in the W==4 path. Also alter the width of o_cnt or o_mem_bytecnt slicing, e.g. o_cnt[3:2] instead of o_cnt[4:3].
bug_categories.applicability: o_cnt is a 3-bit upper counter (bits [4:2]) incremented once per 4-cycle group. An incorrect increment or slice shifts every o_cnt-based decode and gives a wrong o_mem_bytecnt.

bug_categories.bug_type: Control signal polarity / missing term in register file requests
bug_categories.description: Invert or drop a term in o_rf_wreq or o_rf_rreq, e.g. remove `& !trap_pending` from the branch term, swap last_init and o_cnt_done, drop `i_dbus_ack`, or change `i_ibus_ack | trap_pending & last_init` to use `|` / `&` incorrectly.
bug_categories.applicability: o_rf_wreq and o_rf_rreq combine many ops (shift, dbus, MDU, branch, ALU). A mistake causes spurious register writebacks on trapping branches, missed writes for loads or shifts, or missed read requests.

bug_categories.bug_type: FSM state transition error in init_done / ibus_cyc update
bug_categories.description: Change `init_done <= o_init & !init_done` to `o_init | init_done`, change the o_ctrl_jump update to omit o_init, or alter the ibus_cyc enable/value, e.g. `ibus_cyc <= o_ctrl_pc_en` without `| i_rst`, or add or drop terms from the enable condition.
bug_categories.applicability: init_done sequences two-stage ops (init pass, then execute pass) and ibus_cyc controls instruction fetch. Faulty updates cause init_done to stick, jumps to occur in the wrong phase, or the ibus cycle to be missed after reset or completion.

bug_categories.description: Break the conditional features: drop `& !ALIGN` in trap_pending, use `| MDU` instead of `& MDU` in o_mdu_valid, remove the WITH_CSR gate on o_ctrl_trap, or change the misalign_trap_sync_r set/clear logic, e.g. clear on i_ibus_ack without the i_rst term or set without o_init.
bug_categories.applicability: The WITH_CSR, ALIGN and MDU parameters gate the trap and MDU logic. Errors cause traps on aligned-capable configurations, spurious MDU valid, missed misalignment traps, or a latched trap flag that is never cleared.

mutant_rejections.bug_type: FSM state transition error in init_done / ibus_cyc update

bug_categories.description: Change the constant driven onto the output from 1'b0 to 1'b1, so the output is permanently high instead of low.
bug_categories.applicability: The module's sole function is `assign zero = 1'b0;`, so flipping the literal is the most direct functional break and makes the output never match its name.

bug_categories.description: Change the literal width or base, e.g. `assign zero = 2'b10;` or `4'b0001`, so truncation to the 1-bit port gives the wrong value.
bug_categories.applicability: The 1-bit output `zero` receives a sized literal; a wider literal gets truncated to the LSB, which silently yields 0 or 1 depending on the pattern chosen, and a pattern like 2'b01 yields 1.

bug_categories.description: Replace the constant with a high-impedance value, e.g. `assign zero = 1'bz;`, so the output floats instead of being driven low.
bug_categories.applicability: A continuous assign to a single output means the driver is the only source; making it Z removes the defined logic level while remaining valid Verilog.

bug_categories.description: Drive the output with an unknown value, e.g. `assign zero = 1'bx;`, causing X propagation in simulation.
bug_categories.applicability: The constant is the only logic in the design; an X literal compiles cleanly but breaks any downstream checker that expects a deterministic 0.

bug_categories.description: Change the port declaration from `output zero` to `input zero` (or `inout`), which makes the continuous assign illegal or creates a multiple-driver conflict.
bug_categories.applicability: The module has a single output port, so changing its direction breaks the interface and the driver relationship with the parent module.

bug_categories.description: Introduce a new internal wire, e.g. `wire one = 1'b1; assign zero = one;`, or declare an unused wire and assign it the 0 while `zero` gets another value.
bug_categories.applicability: With only one signal, adding an intermediate net that carries the wrong constant, or leaving `zero` driven by the wrong net, changes behavior while staying structurally valid.

bug_categories.description: Replace the literal with an expression that evaluates to 1, such as `assign zero = ~1'b0;` or `!1'b0`.
bug_categories.applicability: A bitwise/logical negation on the constant looks like a plausible coding slip and yields a constant 1 on the `zero` output.

bug_categories.description: Add a second continuous assignment or an always block that also drives `zero` with a different value, e.g. `assign zero = 1'b1;` alongside the original, producing contention (X) on the net.
bug_categories.applicability: The output is a wire driven by a single assign; adding a conflicting driver is valid Verilog that resolves to X in simulation and breaks the constant-0 guarantee.

bug_categories.description: Change the constant driven onto the output from 1'b0 to 1'b1, so the output is permanently high instead of low.
bug_categories.applicability: The module's only behavior is assign out = 1'b0; flipping the literal to 1'b1 is the most direct functional change and is trivially detectable by any test that checks out == 0.

bug_categories.description: Rewrite the assignment as an inverted expression such as assign out = ~1'b0 or assign out = !1'b0, which evaluates to 1.
bug_categories.applicability: Adds an inversion operator to the single continuous assignment, producing a valid but functionally wrong constant-high output.

bug_categories.description: Change the literal to a different width/base such as 1'b0 to 2'b10 or 2'b01, so truncation to the 1-bit output yields an unintended value.
bug_categories.applicability: The output is 1 bit wide; using a multi-bit literal like 2'b01 truncates to 1'b1 (the LSB), silently changing the output while remaining valid Verilog.

bug_categories.description: Replace the constant with 1'bx or 1'bz so the output is undefined or floating rather than a defined logic 0.
bug_categories.applicability: assign out = 1'bz or 1'bx remains legal Verilog and breaks the guarantee of a clean logic-0 output, causing X propagation or tri-state behavior downstream.

bug_categories.description: Introduce an internal wire or reg (e.g., a floating or undriven wire, or a wire tied to 1'b1) and drive out from an expression such as out = 1'b0 | internal_sig.
bug_categories.applicability: Adding an extra undriven or constant-1 internal net ORed into the assignment makes the output either X or 1 despite the module originally having no internal state.

bug_categories.description: Convert the continuous assignment into a clocked or level-sensitive always block that holds or toggles the value, such as an always block that toggles out each evaluation or only updates conditionally.
bug_categories.applicability: Adding an always @(*) block with incomplete assignment (e.g., if (en) out = 0) infers a latch, or a toggling reg makes the formerly constant output time-varying.

bug_categories.description: Alter the output port declaration, such as making it a reg driven by an initial block with the wrong value, or widening it to a multi-bit vector like output [1:0] out.
bug_categories.applicability: Changing out to [1:0] with assign out = 2'b10 or similar changes the interface semantics and the value seen at bit 0 versus the whole vector, breaking the single-bit constant-low contract.

bug_categories.description: Add a second continuous assignment or gate-level driver to out, such as assign out = 1'b1 alongside the original, producing contention that resolves to X.
bug_categories.applicability: Because out is a single wire with one driver, adding a second conflicting driver is a simple, syntactically valid change that yields X on the output in simulation.

bug_categories.description: Change the assigned constant from 1'b1 to 1'b0 so the output is stuck low instead of high.
bug_categories.applicability: The only functional logic is 'assign one = 1'b1;', so flipping the literal directly breaks the module's sole purpose of driving a constant logic high.

bug_categories.description: Replace the constant with 1'bz so the output floats instead of being driven high.
bug_categories.applicability: Assigning 1'bz to 'one' is valid Verilog and leaves the net undriven, which would fail any check expecting a solid logic 1.

bug_categories.description: Replace the constant with 1'bx so the output is an unknown value in simulation.
bug_categories.applicability: The single continuous assignment can be changed to 1'bx, producing an X that propagates to downstream logic and breaks the constant-one guarantee.

bug_categories.description: Widen the output port to a multi-bit vector, e.g. output [1:0] one, while keeping the 1'b1 literal, so the upper bit is zero-extended and the value becomes 2'b01 on a wider bus.
bug_categories.applicability: The port 'one' is declared as a scalar; changing its width alters the interface and the value seen by connecting logic, with the literal 1'b1 being zero-extended into the new width.

bug_categories.description: Change the literal to a multi-bit or differently-sized value such as 1'b1 -> 2'b10 or 1'h0 so truncation yields 0 on the 1-bit output.
bug_categories.applicability: Assigning a wider literal like 2'b10 to a 1-bit output truncates to the LSB (0), silently producing a constant low with no syntax error.

bug_categories.description: Introduce a logical or bitwise negation, e.g. assign one = ~1'b1 or !1'b1, so the output evaluates to 0.
bug_categories.applicability: A unary operator inserted in the single continuous assignment preserves valid syntax yet flips the output to constant zero.

bug_categories.description: Make the output depend on an added input or internal signal, e.g. assign one = en & 1'b1 or a mux, so the output is no longer unconditionally high.
bug_categories.applicability: Adding an input such as 'en' or a signal-dependent ternary turns the constant driver into combinational logic that can drop to 0 and changes the module interface.

bug_categories.description: Replace the continuous assignment with a clocked or latched register (e.g. a flop initialized to 0 or a toggling reg) so the output changes over time or starts low.
bug_categories.applicability: Converting 'one' to a reg driven by an always block that toggles or resets to 0 makes a purely combinational constant into a time-varying output, violating the constant-one behavior.

bug_categories.description: Replace the bitwise NOT with a direct wire connection so the output simply follows the input instead of inverting it.
bug_categories.applicability: Change 'assign out = ~in;' to 'assign out = in;'. The module's only function is inversion, so this makes it a buffer and every output value is wrong.

bug_categories.description: Swap the bitwise NOT operator for a different operator that looks similar, such as logical NOT '!'. For a 1-bit signal this is functionally equivalent, so it is a benign mutation; combined with width changes it can become a real bug.
bug_categories.applicability: Change '~in' to '!in'. It is equivalent for the 1-bit port as declared, so it serves as a control mutation. It becomes a functional bug if the port is widened and the output reduces to a single bit.

bug_categories.description: Drive the output with a constant value, independent of the input, modeling a stuck-at-0 or stuck-at-1 fault.
bug_categories.applicability: Change 'assign out = ~in;' to 'assign out = 1'b0;' or 'assign out = 1'b1;'. The output no longer reacts to 'in', so the inversion is correct for only one of the two input values.

bug_categories.description: Change the port declarations so the input and output have different or wider widths, causing truncation, extension or incorrect inversion semantics.
bug_categories.applicability: Declare 'input [1:0] in' with 'output out' (upper bit dropped), or 'output [1:0] out' so that ~in zero-extends or mismatches in ways that differ from the single-bit inversion.

bug_categories.description: Replace the continuous combinational assignment with a procedural block that infers state, so the output depends on history instead of only on the current input.
bug_categories.applicability: Use 'always @(posedge in) out <= ~in;' with 'output reg out', or a level-sensitive block with incomplete assignment. The output then updates only on certain edges, or holds its value, and does not track the input combinationally.

bug_categories.bug_type: Extra logic gate with hidden dependence
bug_categories.description: Add a second term to the expression, such as an AND or OR with a constant or an internal signal, so the inversion is conditionally masked.
bug_categories.applicability: Change to 'assign out = ~in & 1'b0;' or 'assign out = ~(in | in_dly);', or XOR with a constant, so the output differs from ~in for some input values. Since there is only one input, such masking collapses to constant or buffer behavior.

bug_categories.description: Introduce a wrong connection, such as the output tied to itself or to an undriven net, so the output no longer derives from the input.
bug_categories.applicability: Replace the assignment with 'assign out = ~out;' to create a combinational loop (oscillation or X), or 'assign out = ~in_unused;' where an undeclared or undriven wire leads to X/Z output rather than the inverted input.

bug_categories.description: Apply the inversion an extra time, or in the wrong place, so the net polarity is the opposite of what was intended.
bug_categories.applicability: Change to 'assign out = ~~in;' or 'assign out = ~(~in);'. The two inversions cancel and the module behaves as a buffer, which is functionally identical to inverter removal but a structurally different mutation.

mutants.bug_type: Extra logic gate with hidden dependence

bug_categories.description: Change the concatenation so that only adjacent bit pairs are swapped (e.g., {out[1], out[0], out[3], out[2], ...} = in) instead of a full 8-bit reversal.
bug_categories.applicability: The design's sole function is the bit-reversal mapping in the LHS concatenation; altering the ordering to a pairwise swap yields a valid but functionally different permutation.

bug_categories.description: Reorder the LHS concatenation to {out[7], out[6], ..., out[0]} = in so the output equals the input without reversal.
bug_categories.applicability: A simple reordering of the concatenation list turns the bit-reverser into a pass-through wire, which is syntactically valid and easy to overlook.

bug_categories.description: Replace one index on the LHS with a duplicate (e.g., out[3] listed twice and out[4] omitted), leaving one output bit undriven or multiply driven.
bug_categories.applicability: The LHS concatenation enumerates every output bit explicitly; a copy-paste style index error leaves out[4] floating (Z) and creates a conflict on out[3].

bug_categories.description: Swap just two entries in the concatenation (e.g., out[2] and out[5] positions exchanged) so most bits are reversed correctly but two bits are misrouted.
bug_categories.applicability: Because the mapping is written out manually with 8 entries, exchanging two of them produces a subtle single-pair routing error that only specific input patterns reveal.

bug_categories.description: Narrow the LHS concatenation to fewer than 8 bits (e.g., drop out[7]) or use a partial slice of in, causing truncation and zero-extension/leaving out[7] undriven.
bug_categories.applicability: The assign relies on the 8-bit LHS matching the 8-bit input; removing one element creates a width mismatch with in, changing behavior of the MSB/LSB.

bug_categories.description: Apply a bitwise inversion to the input (e.g., = ~in) or invert a selected portion such as in[3:0], flipping output polarity.
bug_categories.applicability: The combinational assign is a pure wire mapping, so adding a ~ operator on the RHS or a subset is a minimal change that corrupts data values while keeping legality.

bug_categories.description: Split the assignment and tie one or more output bits to a constant (e.g., out[0] = 1'b0) while the remainder is assigned from the corresponding in bits.
bug_categories.applicability: Because the output is a plain 8-bit bus assembled from individual bits, forcing one bit to a constant models a stuck-at fault visible only when the corresponding input bit differs.

bug_categories.bug_type: Wrong bit-order within a half (nibble-level reversal)
bug_categories.description: Reverse bits only within each nibble (e.g., {out[3],out[2],out[1],out[0],out[7],out[6],out[5],out[4]} = in), or swap the upper and lower nibbles without reversing bits internally.
bug_categories.applicability: The 8-bit width splits naturally into two nibbles, so a partially-correct reordering (nibble swap or per-nibble reversal) is a plausible misimplementation that passes simple tests like all-zeros or all-ones.

bug_categories.description: The continuous assignment is changed to drive the logical or bitwise complement of the input, so the output is always the opposite of the input.
bug_categories.applicability: Change 'assign out = in;' to 'assign out = ~in;' or 'assign out = !in;'. Every input value produces the wrong output, and the 1-bit ports make the inversion trivially valid Verilog.

bug_categories.description: The output is tied to a constant 0 or 1 and ignores the input, which models a stuck-at fault on the output net.
bug_categories.applicability: Replace 'assign out = in;' with 'assign out = 1'b0;' or 'assign out = 1'b1;'. The output is correct only when the input happens to match the constant.

bug_categories.description: The output is driven from itself or from an unintended signal instead of the input, creating a combinational loop or an undriven value.
bug_categories.applicability: Change 'assign out = in;' to 'assign out = out;'. The output becomes a combinational loop that resolves to X or Z in simulation instead of following 'in'.

bug_categories.description: A register is inserted in the path so the output lags the input by one clock cycle, turning a purely combinational pass-through into a sequential one.
bug_categories.applicability: Introduce a clock and a flop (e.g. 'always @(posedge clk) out_r <= in;' with out driven from out_r). Output changes are delayed relative to the input, which breaks the zero-latency pass-through contract. This requires adding a clk port or an internal clock.

bug_categories.description: The assignment is rewritten as a conditional always block with incomplete assignment, so the output holds its old value under some conditions instead of tracking the input.
bug_categories.applicability: Replace the assign with 'always @(*) if (in) out_r = 1'b1;' and drive out from out_r. The output latches high and never returns to 0 when the input falls.

bug_categories.description: The output only reflects the input on a certain condition or edge, so some transitions are never propagated.
bug_categories.applicability: Use 'always @(posedge in) out_r <= in;' or gate the assignment with an enable. The rising edge is passed through but falling edges are missed, leaving the output stuck high.

bug_categories.bug_type: Logic gating with an unrelated term
bug_categories.description: An extra operand is combined with the input through AND/OR/XOR, so the output deviates from the input in certain conditions.
bug_categories.applicability: Add an internal signal such as a constant or additional wire: 'assign out = in & en;' or 'assign out = in ^ 1'b1;'. With the extra term at 0 (AND) or 1 (OR), the output no longer follows the input.

bug_categories.description: Port widths or directions are changed so the connection truncates, extends, or mis-drives the data path.
bug_categories.applicability: Declare 'input [1:0] in' with 'output out', so only in[0] reaches out, or make out wider than in so the upper bits are zero-extended. Alternatively, drive out from in[1] only, so the output ignores the actual data bit. Existing testbenches that drive 1-bit values would produce incorrect or X results.

mutants.mutant_code:
module dut
(
  input in,
  output reg out
);


  always @(*) begin
    if(in) begin
      out = in;
    end 
  end


endmodule

bug_categories.description: Replace one of the addition operators with a different operator such as XOR, OR, AND, or subtraction, changing the population-count semantics.
bug_categories.applicability: In 'assign out = in[0] + in[1] + in[2];', changing '+' to '^' makes out equal to the parity of the inputs rather than the count of set bits. Changing to '|' or '&' gives wrong results for inputs with two or three bits set.

bug_categories.description: Drop one of the input bits from the sum so that the output ignores one input.
bug_categories.applicability: Rewriting the expression as 'in[0] + in[1]' (omitting in[2]) or duplicating a bit such as 'in[0] + in[1] + in[1]' makes out wrong whenever the omitted/duplicated bit is 1.

bug_categories.description: Use an incorrect index for one of the input bit selects, so a bit is counted twice and another is not counted.
bug_categories.applicability: Changing 'in[2]' to 'in[1]' or 'in[0]' in the sum causes the design to compute a weighted or partial count; e.g., in=3'b100 would produce 0 instead of 1.

bug_categories.description: Narrow the output width so the MSB of the count is lost.
bug_categories.applicability: Declaring 'output [0:0] out' (or assigning only out[0]) drops the carry bit; inputs with two or three bits set (counts 2 and 3) produce 0 or 1 incorrectly, effectively producing the parity.

bug_categories.description: Swap the significance of the output bits by reversing the output vector range or bit assignment.
bug_categories.applicability: Declaring 'output [0:1] out' or assigning out = {sum[0], sum[1]} swaps the LSB and MSB so count 1 appears as 2 and vice versa, while counts 0 and 3 remain unchanged.

bug_categories.description: Add logic that clamps or alters the result for the maximum-count case.
bug_categories.applicability: Adding a conditional such as 'out = (in == 3'b111) ? 2'b10 : sum' makes the all-ones input produce 2 instead of 3, breaking only that corner case.

bug_categories.description: Change the arithmetic into a form that alters carry propagation or sign handling, such as subtracting a term or using a replicated/signed value.
bug_categories.applicability: Rewriting as 'in[0] + in[1] - in[2]' or using '{in[0]} + {in[1]} + {~in[2]}' modifies the count so that in[2] decrements or inverts, giving wrong counts (e.g., in=3'b100 yields 3 after wraparound in 2 bits).

bug_categories.description: Invert one or more input bits before summation, so the module counts zeros for those bits instead of ones.
bug_categories.applicability: Using '~in[1]' in place of 'in[1]' in the sum means in=3'b000 produces 1 rather than 0 and in=3'b010 produces 0 rather than 1, a subtle failure on specific input patterns.

bug_categories.description: Replace the XOR operator with OR so the expression becomes (x | y) & x, which simplifies to x.
bug_categories.applicability: z = (x ^ y) & x is correct only as x & ~y. Using OR makes z follow x regardless of y, so the case x=1,y=1 yields 1 instead of 0.

bug_categories.description: Replace the outer AND with OR so the expression becomes (x ^ y) | x.
bug_categories.applicability: The output becomes x | y. It is wrong for x=0,y=1 (gives 1 instead of 0) and x=1,y=1 (gives 1 instead of 0).

bug_categories.description: Replace XOR with AND so the expression becomes (x & y) & x, which simplifies to x & y.
bug_categories.applicability: The output is high only when both inputs are 1, which is the exact case where the correct output is 0, and it is low for x=1,y=0 where the correct output is 1.

bug_categories.description: Invert the final result, producing ~((x ^ y) & x).
bug_categories.applicability: The output is complemented for every input combination. z is 1 for x=0 and for x=1,y=1, and 0 only for x=1,y=0.

bug_categories.description: Replace the second use of x in the AND with y, giving (x ^ y) & y.
bug_categories.applicability: This yields y & ~x instead of x & ~y, effectively swapping the roles of the inputs. Output is 1 for x=0,y=1 and 0 for x=1,y=0, the reverse of the correct behavior.

bug_categories.description: Remove or move the parentheses so the expression becomes x ^ (y & x), or equivalently x ^ y & x due to precedence.
bug_categories.applicability: Since & binds tighter than ^, x ^ y & x evaluates as x ^ (y & x) = x & ~y in some cases but differs elsewhere: for x=0,y=1 it gives 0 (correct), but the structure changes and combined with other edits it masks the intended logic. Differences show up when other operators are altered, making the design fragile.

bug_categories.description: Invert one input inside the expression, e.g. (x ^ ~y) & x or (~x ^ y) & x.
bug_categories.applicability: (x ^ ~y) & x gives x & y, which is wrong for x=1,y=0 and x=1,y=1. (~x ^ y) & x also gives x & y. Both change the truth table on the x=1 rows.

bug_categories.description: Replace a sub-expression with a constant, e.g. z = (x ^ 1'b0) & x or z = (x ^ y) & 1'b1.
bug_categories.applicability: The first form reduces to z = x, ignoring y. The second reduces to z = x ^ y, which wrongly outputs 1 for x=0,y=1.

bug_categories.description: Replace the OR inside the inversion with AND, so the gate becomes NAND-like: out = ~(a & b).
bug_categories.applicability: The single expression ~(a | b) is the whole design. Changing | to & gives a 1 output for inputs 00, 01 and 10, so the NOR truth table is broken in two rows.

bug_categories.description: Remove the bitwise NOT so the output becomes a plain OR: out = a | b.
bug_categories.applicability: A NOR is an OR followed by an inversion. Dropping ~ inverts the output for every input combination, so the output is the logical complement of the correct value.

bug_categories.description: Replace | with ^ so out = ~(a ^ b), which is an XNOR.
bug_categories.applicability: XNOR matches NOR for inputs 00 (output 1) and 01/10 (output 0), but differs at 11, where XNOR gives 1 and NOR gives 0. This is a subtle bug that only a single input vector exposes.

bug_categories.description: Swap the bitwise operators for logical ones, e.g. out = !(a || b), or mix them as ~(a || b).
bug_categories.applicability: For 1-bit signals the bitwise and logical forms are functionally identical, so this is an equivalent mutation rather than a functional bug. It is useful as a negative control and checks that the verification does not flag false failures.

bug_categories.description: Use one input twice, e.g. out = ~(a | a), so b is ignored.
bug_categories.applicability: The module has only two inputs, so ignoring b makes out depend only on a. Outputs are wrong whenever b=1 and a=0, where the correct output is 0 but the buggy one is 1.

bug_categories.description: Apply the inversion to only one operand or distribute it incorrectly, e.g. out = ~a | ~b (a NAND) or out = ~a | b.
bug_categories.applicability: A wrong De Morgan rewrite of ~(a | b) should be ~a & ~b. Writing ~a | ~b, or inverting just one input, gives the wrong result on most input combinations.

bug_categories.description: Tie the output to a constant, e.g. assign out = 1'b0 or 1'b1, or force an input to a constant, e.g. ~(a | 1'b0).
bug_categories.applicability: With only a 1-bit output, a stuck-at-0 or stuck-at-1 fault is easy to inject. Stuck-at-0 fails only for input 00; forcing b to 0 makes out ignore b, as in the input-substitution bug.

bug_categories.description: Drive the output from an input or from the wrong signal, e.g. out = ~(a | b) replaced with out = a, out = ~a, or out = ~b.
bug_categories.applicability: The module has only ports a, b and out and no internal signals, so miswiring means routing a single input (possibly inverted) to the output. Both a and b are then not used together, which breaks the two-input NOR function.

bug_categories.description: Remove the outer inversion so the output becomes a ^ b, which inverts the function: out is 1 when inputs differ instead of when they match.
bug_categories.applicability: The assign statement out = ~(a ^ b) is the entire design; dropping the '~' flips every output value across the truth table.

bug_categories.description: Replace the XOR operator with a bitwise AND, giving out = ~(a & b), which is a NAND function.
bug_categories.applicability: out would be 0 only for a=1,b=1 and 1 otherwise, so the output is wrong for inputs 00 (correct) vs 01 and 10 (incorrect, should be 0).

bug_categories.description: Replace the XOR with a bitwise OR, giving out = ~(a | b), which is a NOR function.
bug_categories.applicability: out is 1 only when a=0,b=0; for a=1,b=1 the output becomes 0 instead of the correct 1.

bug_categories.description: Replace the bitwise inversion ~ with the logical negation ! or replace ^ with a logical inequality operator, changing semantics subtly while remaining valid Verilog.
bug_categories.applicability: For 1-bit signals ! and ~ behave the same, but changing ^ to != and keeping ~ would produce ~(a != b) on a 1-bit result, which is still XNOR; combining with ~ misapplied to a 1-bit comparison result (e.g., ~(a == b)) yields XOR, a functional break.

bug_categories.description: Use the same input twice, e.g., out = ~(a ^ a) or out = ~(b ^ b), so the output no longer depends on both inputs.
bug_categories.applicability: With a ^ a always 0, out becomes constant 1, ignoring b entirely; the truth table loses its dependence on one input.

bug_categories.description: Tie the output to a constant (e.g., out = 1'b0 or 1'b1) or mix a constant into the expression such as ~(a ^ 1'b0), which reduces to ~a.
bug_categories.applicability: The module is purely combinational with two inputs; a constant operand makes out depend on only one input or none, producing wrong results for half or all of the input combinations.

bug_categories.description: Move the inversion so it applies to only one operand: out = ~a ^ b, or out = a ^ ~b, instead of inverting the XOR result.
bug_categories.applicability: Mathematically ~a ^ b equals ~(a ^ b) for 1-bit values, but variants such as out = ~a ^ ~b (which equals a ^ b) or out = ~(~a ^ b) (which equals a ^ b) create an XOR instead of XNOR, depending on how inversions are redistributed.

bug_categories.bug_type: Extra logic / dependency on one input only
bug_categories.description: Replace the expression with one that passes through a single input, e.g., out = a or out = ~b, or AND the result with one input like out = ~(a ^ b) & a.
bug_categories.applicability: Adding '& a' makes out 1 only when a=b=1, failing the case a=0,b=0 where XNOR should output 1; this is a realistic gating bug in a tiny combinational function.
